hints: Look at the functional group in the monomer, the C=C double bond tells you this is addition polymerisation, not condensation.
Remember the C=C pi bond breaks open to form two new single bonds, so the backbone becomes $\text{-CH}_2\text{-CH-}$ with the rest of the molecule left as a side chain.
Check that the $\text{-CH}_2\text{OH}$ group stays completely unchanged and attached to one backbone carbon, then find the repeat unit that matches this.
walkthrough:
**Spot the type of polymerisation**

This monomer, $\text{CH}_2=\text{CHCH}_2\text{OH}$, contains an alkene C=C bond. That means it polymerises by addition across the double bond, with no small molecule lost.

General rule:
$$\text{alkene monomer} \rightarrow \text{saturated addition polymer}$$

**Open the double bond**

In addition polymerisation, the pi bond breaks and each C of the C=C gains one new bond to join the chain. The rest of the groups stay exactly as they were.

For this monomer:
$$\text{CH}_2=\text{CHCH}_2\text{OH} \rightarrow \text{-[CH}_2\text{-CH(CH}_2\text{OH})\text{]-}$$

**Build the correct repeat unit**

The backbone must be two carbons long, $\text{-CH}_2\text{-CH-}$, with a $\text{-CH}_2\text{OH}$ side chain on the second carbon. The OH is not directly on the backbone, and there is no C=C or O left in the backbone. This matches only one of the given structures.

options.A: Incorrect. This shows oxygen in the polymer backbone, $\text{-[CH}_2\text{-CH}_2\text{-CH}_2\text{-O]-}$, which would suggest a condensation or ring-opening polymer with loss of atoms. Addition of an alkene never puts O into the main chain.
options.B: Correct. Opening the $\text{CH}_2=\text{CH-}$ double bond gives a saturated $\text{-CH}_2\text{-CH-}$ backbone, leaving the $\text{-CH}_2\text{OH}$ group untouched as a side chain. This is exactly $\text{-[CH}_2\text{-CH(CH}_2\text{OH})\text{]-}$.
options.C: Incorrect. This still contains a C=C double bond in the backbone, $\text{-[CH=C]-}$. In addition polymerisation the pi bond is broken to link monomers together, so the polymer backbone must be fully saturated.
options.D: Incorrect. This shows $\text{-OH}$ directly attached to the backbone, $\text{-[CH}_2\text{-CH}_2\text{-CH(OH)]-}$. The monomer has $\text{-CH}_2\text{OH}$, so the whole $\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ group must remain together as the side chain, not split up.
